annotations.text:
Three directions, same real copy and real numbers.
All at phone width — drivers are the primary audience.

What's fixed in all three: no system fonts, no emoji,
no gradient hero, no uniform card grid.

A — HIGHWAY
Overpass (descended from US highway signage) + Public Sans.
Type IS the graphic. Flat black/white, one orange, thick rules.

For: legible at arm's length in a cab; reads official, which
is its own kind of credible to a safety director.
Against: institutional. Least warm of the three — weakest
where trust is personal.

B — DISPATCH
Archivo + IBM Plex Mono. Bills of lading, dispatch sheets.
Labelled rows, monospace figures, a document header.

For: strongest for carriers — looks like an operation with
real systems, which is exactly what we're selling them.
Against: dense. Hardest to skim on a phone in sunlight,
and the coldest read for a driver.

C — DOBLE VÍA
Bricolage Grotesque + Instrument Sans. One bold orange field.
Spanish and English stacked by construction, not a toggle.

For: strongest for the trokero audience — where the barrier
is trust, not information. Unmistakable in a group chat.
Against: least corporate to a safety director, and it wants
real photography to carry it.

Pick one and I'll build it into the live site.

Or mix: A's hero with C's bilingual treatment is a
real option — the type pairings are the part that
doesn't mix.

Send the graphics whenever; every direction has
room for photography, C most of all.
